To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inhibitory effects of the neuropeptide, CGRP, on the contractility of the mouse myo-uterus are independent of NOS activity.
CGRP inhibits KCl-induced contractile activity of mouse myometrial strips and that this inhibitory effect is independent of NOS isoforms in the mouse uterus.
the inhibitory effect of calcitonin gene-related (CGRP) in the mouse uterus does not depend on the activity of any of the three major isoforms of nitric oxide synthases (NOS).
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel aspect of the CGRP receptor system, namely, the lack of dependence on the activity of NOS isoforms in the mouse uterus.
the role of CGRP and NO in the regulation of myometrial contractility.
the role of CGRP and NO in the regulation of uterine contractility and the results obtained provide new information regarding the role of NOS isoforms in uterine physiology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NO is not the primary messenger for the inhibitory effect of the CGRP on the myometrium.
CGRP does not use the NOS-NO pathway in the myometrial relaxation in mice.
the inhibitory activity of the CGRP on the mouse myometrial contractility is not dependent on the activity of NOS isoforms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CGRP-mediated relaxation of the mouse myo- and non-myo-uterus is independent of NOS activity.
CGRP relaxes the mouse uterus during pregnancy by a mechanism that is independent of the NOS activity.
CGRP inhibits myometrium in a manner independent of NOS activity and the inhibitory effect of this peptide is dependent on the stage of gestation and the hormonal milieu.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NO is not involved in the relaxation of mouse uterus by CGRP.
the inhibitory effect of the neuropeptide, CGRP, is not mediated by NO.
NO is not involved in the inhibitory action exerted by CGRP on uterotonic activity.
